The issue description says: "A heap-buffer-overflow occurs in format_expand1 due to incorrect handling of the terminal '#' character. The code checks the current byte and advances the pointer, then dereferences the pointer in the loop header, reading one byte past the end of the heap buffer."

Looking at the code:
```c
while (*fmt != '\0') {        // line 5457 - loop header dereferences fmt
    if (*fmt != '#') {        // line 5458
        ...
        buf[off++] = *fmt++; // line 5463
        continue;
    }
    if (*fmt++ == '\0')      // line 5466 - checks current byte AND advances pointer
        break;

    ch = (u_char)*fmt++;     // line 5469 - dereferences fmt again
    switch (ch) {
    ...
```

The bug: When `fmt` points to a `'#'` that is the LAST character before the null terminator (i.e., the string ends with `#`), here's what happens:

1. `while (*fmt != '\0')` - `*fmt` is `'#'`, not `'\0'`, so we enter the loop. (line 5457)
2. `if (*fmt != '#')` - false, since `*fmt` is `'#'`. (line 5458)
3. `if (*fmt++ == '\0')` - `*fmt` is `'#'` (not `'\0'`), so the condition is false. But `fmt++` advances `fmt` to now point at the `'\0'` terminator. (line 5466)
4. `ch = (u_char)*fmt++;` - `*fmt` is now `'\0'` (the null terminator). `ch` becomes 0. `fmt++` advances `fmt` to point ONE PAST the null terminator (past the end of the buffer). (line 5469)
5. `switch (ch)` - ch is 0, falls to `default` case.
6. In the default case, `s = NULL` initially. Then `if (fmt > style_end)` - style_end is NULL, so fmt (which is past the buffer) > NULL is true. Then checks `ch >= 'A' && ch <= 'Z'` - ch is 0, false. `ch >= 'a' && ch <= 'z'` - false. So s stays NULL.
7. `if (s == NULL)` - true. So it does `buf[off++] = '#'; buf[off++] = ch;` (writes '#' and 0). Then `continue`.
8. Back to `while (*fmt != '\0')` - now `fmt` points ONE PAST the null terminator, which is past the end of the heap buffer. This dereferences memory past the buffer → heap-buffer-overflow READ.

So the trigger input is simply a string that ends with `#`. The simplest PoC is just `#` (a single hash character).
